about: Baseball's defaults, as data (docs/PLAN-start-a-game-gpt.md track L, L1): a sport's standard scoring, categories, lineup slots and locks, and the game specs a sport's Make it a game starts from instead of asking the bot. Stat keys are Baseball's (src/lib/sports/baseball.ts); slots take its positions or position groups. The specs are in the game spec's shape (A1's schema, on the engine branch); slots and categories aren't in that schema yet (L4 adds them), so they're kept beside it for the spec to read.
finalSource: Step 2.7 (docs/PLAN-sports-ready.md): the final a game through the playoffs runs to, as people name it ("Through the Super Bowl"); words for 4.0's pass

scoring.source: ESPN's standard points league for baseball

ir.source: Yahoo's default roster's 4 IL, outside its 23, for someone his team has put on the injured list (help.yahoo.com/kb/SLN6785.html, SLN6425.html, 2026-11-20)

eligible.source: Yahoo's and ESPN's: a player fills each position he plays, not only his roster's one. ESPN's roster lists the positions each has played; a player counts at each in his own group (a shortstop listed at second base fills 2B, a reliever listed as a starter fills SP), and a batter listed as a starting pitcher (a two-way player: Shohei Ohtani) at the pitchers' too. Not a batter listed as a reliever: a position player who pitched in a blowout.

waivers.source: Yahoo's public defaults: a continual rolling list, roster changes Daily - Today, at most 6 acquisitions a week (help.yahoo.com/kb/SLN6785.html, 2026-11-20). Claims clear each game day's morning, 12 hours before its first game, then free agents until its last game starts (BACKLOG 219; docs/PLAN-sports-ready.md step 2.5)

pace.source: The user's rule (2026-11-19, BACKLOG 218), by the day for baseball (2026-11-20: doubleheaders): a seat at its own pace has watched the games before once a game on a later day starts, so a doubleheader's first isn't marked watched at the second's first pitch (docs/PLAN-sports-ready.md step 2.6)

season.about: A season-long league: draft a full roster, set a daily lineup, play someone head to head each week.

short.about: One game, a series or a team's next few: everyone drafts a few players, every one of them scores, most points wins.

pickem.about: Each game, before it starts: who wins? A point for each one right, most points wins (a tie counts for nobody).

pickAFew.about: Each game, before it starts: pick three players. 3 points for each one who has the most total bases in the game (tied, each of them), most points wins.

ask.ask: Pick three: who has the most total bases?

categories.about: A season-long league by categories: draft a full roster, set a daily lineup, play someone head to head in Yahoo's 5x5's ten categories: each category you win is a win.

roto.about: A season-long league, roto-style: draft a full roster, set a daily lineup; each of Yahoo's 5x5's ten categories ranks everyone over the season, points by rank, most points wins.

bestBall.about: Best ball: draft a full roster and never set a lineup: each game, your best eighteen count, most points wins.

bracket.about: A playoff bracket: before the MLB playoffs start, pick who wins every series, round by round to the World Series. A point for each one right in the first round, doubling each round after it; most points wins.

ask.ask: Who wins every series of the MLB playoffs?
